sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Weert charges for street parking in two zones in the centre and keeps a permit-only zone 3 around it. Under the 2023 designation decision, paid street parking in zones 1 and 2 runs Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 18:00, seven car parks charge round the clock and permit-only zone 3 covers about 66 streets, among them Parallelweg, Spoorstraat and Maaseikerweg [5]. The municipal parking page says no payment is needed on the street on Thursday shopping evenings, shopping Sundays and public holidays, and that disabled badge holders may park free for up to three hours with a disc on general disabled bays, but not in garages [7]. Residents in zones 1 and 2 may receive at most two street permits per address, and in zone 3 at most three, minus any private space or driveway, and for some centre addresses no street permit is issued; employees can get only a zone 2 permit, and the municipality says residents cannot expect to park in front of their door [8]. The hours of zone 3 are worded slightly differently in the 2023 decision and the 2026 table, so the exact current hours should be checked [6]. From 1 October 2026 the Weerterlandpas and Stadsparkeren card readers for street parking stop working because the 2G network is being phased out; this was announced on 10 August 2026, and nothing changes for other parkers [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The station area is the one big development, and nothing is decided. At a public meeting on 5 October 2026 with 33 participants the municipality presented a first picture with a possible car-free station square, a new southern station entrance and a tunnel for car traffic, and the report says these are not decisions [17]. At the Spoorzone festival on 5 March 2026, with 120 participants, residents said they found it hard to imagine parking in hubs and worried about where cars will park with many new homes; the council was then expected to discuss the vision in May or June 2026, and we did not find the outcome [18]. Public charge points sit inside the car parks: 10 in Centrumgarage, 4 in Ursulinengarage, 4 in Walburgpassage and 2 each in Poort van Limburg and Muntgarage, with none listed for Stationspleingarage [13].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality runs six garages and the Centrum-Noord lot, all at the same rates [9]. The 2026 tariff is 1.70 euros an hour and 6.60 euros a day, round the clock, the same as in 2025 [0][2], and the enforcement surcharge is 82.00 euros, up from 78.80 [1]. A 24/7 garage subscription costs 600 euros a year, an OV-traveller subscription 504 euros, and the Centrum-Noord subscription rose to 313.90 euros; a resident street permit costs 156.95 euros in zones 1 and 2 [3]. Digital visitor parking in zone 3 costs 0.15 euros an hour for residents' visitors [4]. The 500-hour employee bundle, at 100 euros, is temporarily unavailable at Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage and Poort van Limburg because of high parking pressure, and Poort van Limburg has a waiting list [12]. The park-and-ride at Parallelweg is run by Q-Park and not by the municipality; Q-Park's page shows 295 spaces, open round the clock, with an NS discount, but its tariffs did not load [9][10]. Permits and bundles are managed through a digital desk, and mobile payment through ParkerenPlus [19].

Our data cover the Parallelweg park-and-ride, whose feed gives 477 spaces against the 295 on Q-Park's page, so the percentages are approximate. Over about 61 days since 22 August 2026 occupancy averaged about 50% on weekdays and 44% at weekends, and the car park reached nearly full in single readings, on a Saturday evening among others. The municipal garages are not in our data.
